purpose: Preserve medium-hole and large-hole opportunities without treating all prices as one regime. This design is a research candidate only and does not access or score live odds/results under CURRENT v91.
principle: Separate price regimes because a small absolute probability error is much more dangerous at very high odds.
Require stronger model-vs-market evidence as the odds band rises.
Keep longshot exposure sparse: at most one elementary longshot ticket per race per lane.
Never chase losses or enlarge stake after losses.
Validation must reward repeated edge, not one jackpot.

proposed_price_regimes.extra_rule: Research-only until sufficient prospective calibration exists; no promotion from a single hit.

probability_guard.conservative_probability: min(S0-derived ticket probability, challenger-derived ticket probability)
probability_guard.no_hindsight: all inputs must be timestamped before the declared decision cutoff when odds access is separately authorized

race_level_controls.precedence: If multiple bands qualify, rank by guarded_edge_ratio but respect total risk cap; do not add tickets merely to increase hit coverage.

metrics: largest single-hit share of total profit
anti_jackpot_gate: A candidate cannot be called stable if total profit becomes negative after removing its largest hit.
A candidate cannot be promoted on one isolated winning ticket.
Mid/longshot/extreme regimes must be reported separately rather than pooled into one flattering ROI.

rationale: The thresholds are deliberately monotone with odds: higher-payout tickets require a larger probability advantage and receive less shadow risk. They are engineering starting points, not claims of optimality.
